title: Geometry and Constants in Finite Ring Continuum

rows.label: A1
rows.predicate: Finite-field algebra: $\Fpx$ is cyclic of order $\p-1$; its generators are the $\gen^{u}$, $u\in\Zp^{\times}$; $\gen^{(\p-1)/2}=-1$; $-1$ is a square in $\Fp$ iff $\p\equiv1\pmod4$; the fourth roots of unity form the unique subgroup of order four (1:A2, 1:A3, 1:B2).

rows.label: A2
rows.predicate: The sign of the quarter-turn exponent: $\im=\gen^{-\kap}=-\gen^{\kap}$, the exponent negative by pullback covariance (00:C7); the positive-exponent reading is the conjugate chart. Declared here, derived in the corpus.

rows.label: A3
rows.predicate: Topology: a closed connected surface with Euler characteristic $2$ is the two-sphere; the suspension of a circle is $S^{2}$ (Hatcher, Ex.~0.14); a quotient of a regular CW complex by a subcomplex is a CW complex.

rows.label: A4
rows.predicate: The framed-rational charts of 1-algebra: the window law for framed rationals and the scale grid's cover of the field; on one shell the scale grids $x/\gen^{n}$, $|x|\le2\kap$, trade range for resolution (1:D8, 1:D9).

rows.label: A5
rows.predicate: Breusch's bound: for every $x\ge7$ a prime $\p\equiv1\pmod4$ lies in $(x,2x]$.

rows.label: B1
rows.predicate: The shell $(\kap,\Fp)$, capacity-first: $\kap$ primary, $\p=4\kap+1$ prime; the half-period $\pi:=2\kap$; the meridian steps $I_{\p}=\{0,\dots,\pi\}$; the phase cycle $\Phi_{\p}\cong C_{\p-1}$, $m\mapsto\gen^{m}$ (00:C1).

rows.label: B2
rows.predicate: The frame $\Fp(\chron;0,1,\gen)$: origin, unit, and the frame's drive generator $\gen$, a primitive generator of $\Fpx$; $\chron$ the chronon (00:C1, convention~3).

rows.label: B3
rows.predicate: Primitive generators form one orbit: every generator is $\gen^{u}$ with $u\in\Zp^{\times}$, a torsor for $\operatorname{Aut}(C_{\p-1})$.
rows.name: primitive_generators_one_orbit

rows.label: B4
rows.predicate: Cellular automorphisms of the index grid: $m\mapsto\pm m+c$, the dihedral group of the phase cycle; on the completion also meridian reversal $a\mapsto\pi-a$, exchanging the poles. The reindexing $\rho_{u}\colon m\mapsto um$ preserves latitude adjacency only for $u\equiv\pm1\pmod{\p-1}$; $\sigma$ is not a map of $\Sp$ ($\north$ one vertex, $L_{\pi}$ has $\p-1$).
rows.name: cellular_automorphisms_index_grid

blocks.title: The orbital shell and its completion

rows.label: C1
rows.predicate: The orbital shell $\Sp$: vertices $\north$ and $v_{a,m}$ ($1\le a\le\pi$, $m\in\Phi_{\p}$), meridian and latitude edges, north triangles, quadrilaterals. The action reading $v_{a,m}\equiv a\gen^{m}$ is $\pi$-to-one onto $\Fpx$: the surface is two-faced (00:B11, 1:C4).

rows.label: C2
rows.predicate: Counts: $|V|=\pi(\p-1)+1$, $|E|=2\pi(\p-1)$, $|F|=\pi(\p-1)$, $\chi(\Sp)=1$; the completion has $(\pi-1)(\p-1)+2$ vertices, $(2\pi-1)(\p-1)$ edges, $\pi(\p-1)$ faces, $\chi=2$.
rows.name: cell_counts

rows.label: C3
rows.predicate: Canonical spherical completion: collapsing $L_{\pi}$ to $\south$ gives a closed orientable surface --- every edge in two faces, every vertex link a cycle --- with $\chi=2$, hence $S^{2}$ (A3), on every shell.
rows.name: canonical_spherical_completion

rows.label: C4
rows.predicate: Frame covariance: $\Sp$ is one complex for every generator --- the index grid $I_{\p}\times\Phi_{\p}$ with its step relations; the frame $\gen'=\gen^{u}$ moves the field labels, $a\gen^{m}\mapsto a\gen^{um}$, by the automorphism $\rho_{u}$ of $\Phi_{\p}$, not the cells. The reindexing $\varphi_{u}$ is cellular only for $u\equiv\pm1$.
rows.source: Prop.~\ref{prop:shell-covariance}; rests on C1, B4\newline \pywit{geometry}{p02012}{C4}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p02012}{C4} \lean{FRC.Geometry.label\_covariance, FRC.Geometry.rho\_adj\_iff}
rows.name: frame_covariance

rows.label: C5
rows.predicate: The edge metric of the completion: the distance between the vertices of latitudes $a,a'$ and phases $m,m'$ is $\min(|a-a'|+\delta(m,m'),a+a',2\pi-a-a')$, with $\delta$ the cyclic distance on $\Phi_{\p}$ and $\delta=0$ at a pole; shortest paths follow a meridian and a latitude or pass through a pole; the diameter is $\pi$.
rows.name: edge_metric

rows.label: C6
rows.predicate: Curvature of the completion, $K(v)=1-\deg v/2+\sum_{f\ni v}1/|f|$, for $\p\ge13$: zero at every vertex of latitude $2\le a\le\pi-2$, $1/6$ on the latitudes $1$ and $\pi-1$, $1-(\p-1)/6$ at each pole; the total is $2$.
rows.name: completion_curvature

rows.label: C7
rows.predicate: The flat band, for $\p\ge13$: for $2r\le a\le\pi-2r$ the ball of radius $r$ about a vertex of latitude $a$ is isometric to the ball of radius $r$ of the square lattice; the observer origin, with $\p-1$ neighbours and nonzero curvature, has no flat ball.
rows.name: flat_band

blocks.title: The Euclidean datum and the involutions

rows.label: D1
rows.predicate: The half-period: $\gen^{\pi}=-1$ for every primitive $\gen$, $\pi=2\kap$; $2\pi\equiv-1$ (00:C1).
rows.name: half_period_is_minus_one

rows.label: D2
rows.predicate: The quarter-turn subgroup $\Qp=\{x:x^{4}=1\}$ is the unique subgroup of order four; $\gen^{\kap}$ has order four with $(\gen^{\kap})^{2}=-1$; $\Qp=\{\pm1,\pm\im\}$ (1:B2).
rows.source: Prop.~\ref{prop:quarter-turn}; rests on D1; Def.~\ref{def:quarter-turn-subgroup}\newline \pywit{geometry}{p02014}{D2}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p02014}{D2}, \leanwit{FrcMathlib}{p02014}{D2} \lean{Geometry.quarter\_turn\_order, FRC.Shell.Frame.quarter\_turn\_order, FRC.Shell.Frame.fourth\_roots}
rows.name: quarter_turn_subgroup_unique

rows.label: D3
rows.predicate: The oriented quarter-turn $\im=-\gen^{\kap}=\gen^{-\kap}$, $\im^{2}=-1$, orientation by A2; on $\F_{13}(\chron;0,1,2)$: $\im=5$, $-\im=8$, $\pi=6$ [value] (Fig.~\ref{fig:f13-constant-datum}).
rows.name: quarter_turn_orientation

rows.label: D4
rows.predicate: The exponential unit $\eu:=\gen^{\im}$, $\im$ read as an exponent in $\Phi_{\p}$ through its residue representative; derived, generator-dependent (00:C1, convention~3); on $\F_{13}$, $\eu=6=\pi$ [value].

rows.label: D5
rows.predicate: Orientation classes: for $\gen'=\gen^{u}$, $\im'=-\gen'^{\kap}$ equals $\im$ when $u\equiv1\pmod4$ and $-\im$ when $u\equiv3\pmod4$; the oriented quarter-turn is frame-covariant within one class of generators, not under every generator change.
rows.name: orientation_classes

rows.label: D6
rows.predicate: The Euler identity on the shell: $\eu^{\im\pi}=\gen^{2\kap\im^{2}}=(-1)^{\im}$, equal to $-1$ exactly when the representative of $\im$ is odd (00:C14); the oriented frames of a shell are those with $-\gen^{\kap}$ odd --- on $\F_{13}$, $\gen=2$ ($\im=5$) is one and $\gen=7$ ($\im=8$) is not.
rows.name: euler_identity_shell

rows.label: D7
rows.predicate: Negation $R(x)=-x$ and inversion $I(x)=x^{-1}$ are commuting involutions; off $\Qp$ the $\langle R,I\rangle$-orbit $\{x,-x,x^{-1},-x^{-1}\}$ has four elements, and $\Fpx\setminus\Qp$ splits into $\kap-1$ such orbits (1:B2).
rows.name: negation_inversion_commute

rows.label: D8
rows.predicate: Euclidean conjugation $C_{\gen}\colon(a,b)\mapsto(a,-b)$ is an involution of the coordinate pairs $\Fp^{2}$; on the shell $a+b\im$ is a field element and the pair map $\Fp^{2}\to\Fp$ is $\p$-to-one (1:E2), so $C_{\gen}$ is a chart-level involution, not a field automorphism.

rows.label: E1
rows.predicate: The comparison map $\Xi_{\p,\gen}$ [chart]: $\north\mapsto(0,0,1)$, $v_{a,m}\mapsto(\sin\theta_{a}\cos\phi_{m},\sin\theta_{a}\sin\phi_{m},\cos\theta_{a})$ with $\theta_{a}=\pi_{\R}a/(2\kap)$, $\phi_{m}=2\pi_{\R}m/(\p-1)$, $\pi_{\R}$ the chart constant (00:N2); $L_{\pi}\mapsto(0,0,-1)$.

rows.label: E2
rows.predicate: Base-grid estimate [chart]: every point of $S^{2}$ lies within geodesic distance $\delta_{\p}=\sqrt2\,\pi_{\R}/(\p-1)$ of $\Xi_{\p,\gen}(V(\Sp))$; in counts, every latitude fraction and every phase fraction rounds to a grid index within half a step. Measured covering radius $0.36$ at $\p=13$, bound $0.370$.
rows.name: base_grid_rounding

rows.label: E3
rows.predicate: Fixed-shell refinement is bounded: with $\gen^{m}\le2\kap+1<\gen^{m+1}$ no point $x/\gen^{n}$, $0\le x\le2\kap$, lies in $(\max(1-\gen^{-m},2\kap\gen^{-m-1}),1)$ at any depth, so the covering radius of the scale grids in $[0,1]$ is $\ge\tfrac12\min(\gen^{-m},1-2\kap\gen^{-m-1})\ge1/(\p+1)$: $1/8$ at $(13,2)$, $5/22$ at $(13,11)$.
rows.name: fixed_shell_refinement_bounded

rows.label: E4
rows.predicate: Precision at the shell's resolution [chart]: for every $L$-bounded observable family and configuration on $(S^{2})^{r}$, vertex images of $\Sp$ reproduce every observable within $L^{2}\delta_{\p}$; a tolerance $\varepsilon$ is met on every shell with $\p-1>\sqrt2\,\pi_{\R}L^{2}/\varepsilon$, and one such shell has $\p\le2\max(7,\sqrt2\,\pi_{\R}L^{2}/\varepsilon+1)$ (A5).
rows.source: Thm.~\ref{thm:operational-precision}; rests on E2; A5\newline \pywit{geometry}{p02024}{E4}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p02024}{E4} \lean{FRC.Shell.Frame.round\_exists, FRC.Geometry.lipschitz\_budget}
rows.name: precision_shell_resolution

blocks.title: Fourier duality on the phase cycle

rows.label: F1
rows.predicate: $\gen$ is a principal $n$-th root of unity, $n=\p-1$: $\gen^{n}=1$, $\sum_{j<n}\gen^{jk}=0$ for $0<k<n$, and $n^{-1}=-1$ in $\Fp$ ($2\pi\equiv-1$).
rows.name: principal_root_of_unity

rows.label: F2
rows.predicate: The ring Fourier transform on the phase cycle: $\mathcal F_{\gen}(v)_{k}=\sum_{j<n}v_{j}\gen^{jk}$ on $V_{\gen}=\Fp^{n}$; the matrix $(W_{\gen})_{kj}=\gen^{jk}$.

rows.label: F3
rows.predicate: Inversion: $v_{j}=-\sum_{k<n}\mathcal F_{\gen}(v)_{k}\gen^{-jk}$, i.e.\ $W_{\gen}^{-1}=-(\gen^{-jk})_{jk}=-W_{\gen}J$ (6:B5), exact on every shell.
rows.name: dft_inversion

rows.label: F4
rows.predicate: Polynomial reading: $\mathcal F_{\gen}(v)_{k}=P_{v}(\gen^{k})$ with $P_{v}=\sum_{j}v_{j}X^{j}$; the transform exchanges coefficients with values on the phase cycle.
rows.name: polynomial_reading

rows.label: F5
rows.predicate: Covariance under generator change: for $\gen'=\gen^{u}$, $v^{(\gen')}_{j}=v^{(\gen)}_{uj}$ and $\mathcal F_{\gen'}(v^{(\gen')})=\mathcal F_{\gen}(v^{(\gen)})$.
rows.name: covariance_generator_change

rows.label: F6
rows.predicate: Exact external transport [chart]: $\chi(\gen^{m})=e^{-2\pi_{\R}im/n}$ is an isomorphism of $\Fpx$ onto the complex $n$-th roots of unity with $\chi(\gen^{m+1})=e^{-2\pi_{\R}i/n}\chi(\gen^{m})$, $\chi(\gen^{m+\pi})=-\chi(\gen^{m})$, $\chi(\im\gen^{m})=i\,\chi(\gen^{m})$; in the exponents, $\gen^{m+\pi}=-\gen^{m}$ and $\im\gen^{m}=\gen^{m+3\kap}$.
rows.name: external_transport_exponents

rows.label: F7
rows.predicate: The large-$\p$ reading [chart]: the phase cycle read as the $n$-point grid $\phi_{m}=2\pi_{\R}m/n$ on $S^{1}$; the classical sampled DFT, exact recovery for $n>2N$, and the trapezoidal rule's geometric convergence in $n$ are the degenerate comparison case, imported.

B3.name: FRC.Geometry.generator_orbit
B3.doc: 2:B3 (Props. 2.7, 4.5, the primitive generators form one orbit): the primitive roots of unity of order `n = card F − 1` are exactly the `g^u` with `u < n` coprime to `n`.

B3.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.generator_orbit
B3.doc: 2:B3 (Props. 2.7, 4.5), 1-algebra's torsor — the primitive generators form one orbit: `h` is primitive of order `p − 1` exactly when `h = g^u` for some `u < p − 1` coprime to `p − 1`.

B3.name: FRC.Shell.s13_orbit
B3.doc: 2:B3 [value] — on `𝔽₁₃` the generators are `2^u` with `u ∈ {1, 5, 7, 11}` (the units mod `12`): `6 = 2^5` is primitive, `4 = 2^2` is not; `5, 7, 11` are invertible mod `12`, `2` is not.

B4.name: FRC.Geometry.rho_adj_iff
B4.doc: 2:B4, 2:C4 (Prop. 2.8) — `ρ_u` preserves the adjacency of the phase cycle (`n ≥ 3`) exactly when `u ≡ 1` or `u ≡ −1 (mod n)`.

B4.name: FRC.Geometry.rotation_adj
B4.doc: 2:B4 — the rotations `m ↦ m + c` preserve adjacency (with `ρ_{±1}` they generate the dihedral maps of B4).

B4.name: FRC.Complex.census13
B4.doc: 2:B4, 2:C4 [value] — on `𝔽₁₃` (`n = 12`) the reindexing `ρ_u` is cellular exactly for `u ∈ {1, 11}` among the units `{1, 5, 7, 11}`, and the pole exchange is cellular on the completion.

C2.name: FRC.Geometry.euler_characteristic
C2.doc: 2:C2 (Remark 3.4, the counts): for the orbital shell, `χ = V − E + F = 1`; for its completion, `χ = 2` (`π = 2κ`, `n = p − 1`), as integer identities.

C2.name: FRC.Geometry.euler_characteristic
C2.doc: 2:C2, 2:C3, 2:C6 (Remark 3.4) — the counts: with `π = m + 1` phases-deep and `n = p − 1` phases, `|V| − |E| + |F| = 1` for the shell and `2` for its completion, written without subtraction: `(πn + 1) + πn = 2πn + 1` and `((π−1)n + 2) + πn = (2π−1)n + 2`.

C2.name: FRC.Complex.counts13
C2.doc: 2:C2 [value] — the counts on `𝔽₁₃`: `62` vertices, `72` faces of the completion.

C3.name: FRC.Geometry.euler_characteristic
C3.doc: 2:C2, 2:C3, 2:C6 (Remark 3.4) — the counts: with `π = m + 1` phases-deep and `n = p − 1` phases, `|V| − |E| + |F| = 1` for the shell and `2` for its completion, written without subtraction: `(πn + 1) + πn = 2πn + 1` and `((π−1)n + 2) + πn = (2π−1)n + 2`.

C3.name: FRC.Complex.closed13
C3.doc: 2:C3 [value] — the completion is a closed surface on `𝔽₁₃` (62 vertices, 72 faces).

C3.name: FRC.Complex.open13
C3.doc: 2:C3, 2:B4 [value] — the shell itself is not closed (its terminal latitude is a boundary: those sides lie in one face only), so the meridian reversal has nothing to act on before the collapse.

C4.name: FRC.Geometry.label_covariance
C4.doc: 2:C4 (Prop. 3.5) — the complex is one for every generator; the frame `g' = g^u` moves the labels by the reindexing `ρ_u`: `label g' (a, m) = label g (a, u·m mod n)`.

C4.name: FRC.Geometry.rho_adj_iff
C4.doc: 2:B4, 2:C4 (Prop. 2.8) — `ρ_u` preserves the adjacency of the phase cycle (`n ≥ 3`) exactly when `u ≡ 1` or `u ≡ −1 (mod n)`.

C5.name: FRC.Complex.metric13
C5.doc: 2:C5, 2:C7 [value] — on `𝔽₁₃` the distance formula is the graph distance of the completion: for every source `s` it vanishes at `s`, changes by at most one along every edge, and every other vertex has a neighbour one step closer. These three properties characterise the distance from `s` (induction on the formula's value). The diameter is `π = 6`, between the poles.

C6.name: FRC.Complex.curvature13
C6.doc: 2:C6 [value] — on `𝔽₁₃` the curvature: zero on the band `2 ≤ a ≤ π − 2`, `1/6` on the latitudes `1` and `π − 1`, `1 − (p − 1)/6 = −1` at each pole (twelve times: `0`, `2`, `−12`); the total is `24/12 = 2`, the Euler characteristic.

C6.name: FRC.Geometry.euler_characteristic
C6.doc: 2:C2, 2:C3, 2:C6 (Remark 3.4) — the counts: with `π = m + 1` phases-deep and `n = p − 1` phases, `|V| − |E| + |F| = 1` for the shell and `2` for its completion, written without subtraction: `(πn + 1) + πn = 2πn + 1` and `((π−1)n + 2) + πn = (2π−1)n + 2`.

C7.name: FRC.Complex.flat13
C7.doc: 2:C7 [value] — on `𝔽₁₃` the band is a square grid: every vertex with `2 ≤ a ≤ 4` has four neighbours, pairwise at distance two (the unit ball of the square lattice), while each pole has `p − 1 = 12` neighbours.

C7.name: FRC.Complex.metric13
C7.doc: 2:C5, 2:C7 [value] — on `𝔽₁₃` the distance formula is the graph distance of the completion: for every source `s` it vanishes at `s`, changes by at most one along every edge, and every other vertex has a neighbour one step closer. These three properties characterise the distance from `s` (induction on the formula's value). The diameter is `π = 6`, between the poles.

D1.name: FRC.Geometry.half_period
D1.doc: 2:D1 (Prop. 4.1, the shell half-period): `g^π = −1` for `π = 2κ` and every primitive root `g`.

D1.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.half_period
D1.doc: 2:D1, 13:H2, 00:C1 — the half-period: `g^{2κ} = −1` for the drive of every frame (the half-turn tautology behind `χ(−1) = e^{iπ}`).

D2.name: FRC.Geometry.quarter_turn_order
D2.doc: 2:D2 (Prop. 4.3, the quarter-turn structure): `i = −g^κ` squares to `−1`, so `g^κ` has order four.

D2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.fourth_roots
D2.doc: 1:B2, 2:D2 (Theorem 1, the structural set) — the fourth roots of unity are exactly `1, −1, i, −i`.

D5.name: FRC.Geometry.orientation_class
D5.doc: 2:D5 (Remark 4.11 — the orientation classes): under `g' = g^u` the oriented quarter-turn `i' = −g'^κ` equals `i = −g^κ` when `u ≡ 1 (mod 4)` and `−i` when `u ≡ 3 (mod 4)`.

D5.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.orientation_class
D5.doc: 2:D5, 6:B3, 13:B2 — the orientation classes: for `g' = g^u`, the quarter-turn `−g'^κ` is `−g^κ` when `u ≡ 1 (mod 4)` and `−(−g^κ)` when `u ≡ 3 (mod 4)`.

D6.name: FRC.Geometry.euler_identity
D6.doc: 2:D6 (the Euler identity on the shell, master C14): with `e = g^i` and `π = 2κ`, `e^(iπ) = (−1)^i` for any integer reading `i` of the quarter-turn — `−1` exactly when that reading is odd.

D6.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.euler_identity
D6.doc: 2:D6, 6:B2, 00:C14 — the Euler identity on the shell: with `e = g^i` and `π = 2κ`, `(g^i)^{i·2κ} = (−1)^i` for every natural reading `i` of the quarter-turn — `−1` exactly when `i` is odd.

D6.name: FRC.Geometry.s13_orientation
D6.doc: 2:D6 [value] — on `𝔽₁₃` the frame `g = 2` reads `i = 5` (odd: `e^{iπ} = −1`) and the frame `g = 7` reads `i = 8` (even: `e^{iπ} = +1`); `7 = 2^{11}` with `11 ≡ 3 (mod 4)` flips the orientation.

D7.name: FRC.Algebra.klein_orbit_four
D7.doc: 1:B2 (Theorem 1, orbit clause), 2:D7: for a unit `x` with `x² ≠ 1` and `x² ≠ −1` the four elements `x, −x, x⁻¹, −x⁻¹` of the Klein-four orbit are pairwise distinct (any field of characteristic `≠ 2`); the structural set `{1, i, −1, −i}` is exactly the complement.

D7.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.klein_orbit_four
D7.doc: 1:B2 (Theorem 1 of 1-algebra), 2:D7 — off the fourth roots of unity, `x`, `−x`, `x⁻¹`, `−x⁻¹` are four distinct residues (`y` stands for the inverse: `x·y = 1`).

D7.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.orbit_rep
D7.doc: 1:B2 (Theorem 1, the count, existence), 2:D7 — every residue off `Q₄` lies in the Klein orbit of some `g^r` with `1 ≤ r < κ`.

D7.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.orbit_rep_unique
D7.doc: 1:B2 (Theorem 1, the count, uniqueness), 2:D7 — two representatives `g^r`, `g^{r'}` with `1 ≤ r, r' < κ` whose orbits meet are the same: the Klein orbits off `Q₄` are exactly `κ − 1`, one for each `r ∈ [1, κ)`.

E2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.round_exists
E2.doc: 1:E4, 2:E2, 2:E4 — every framed turn has its rounding (the division with remainder by `2v`).

E3.name: FRC.Geometry.fixed_shell_bound
E3.doc: 2:E3 (the fixed-shell bound, every shell): for any depth cut `m`, every grid point `x / g^n` with `x ≤ 2κ` that lies below `1` is at most `max (1 − g^{−m}) (2κ · g^{−(m+1)})`; with `m = ⌊log_g(2κ+1)⌋` that bound is below `1` (`fixed_shell_bound_lt_one`), so the interval above it is free at every depth and the covering radius of the fixed-shell refinement in `[0, 1]` is bounded below independently of `N`.

E3.name: FRC.Geometry.fixed_shell_bound
E3.doc: 2:E3 (the fixed-shell bound, every shell) — for `g ≥ 2`, any cut `m`, depth `n` and `x ≤ 2κ` with `x < g^n` (the grid point `x/g^n` below `1`): either `x/g^n ≤ 1 − g^{−m}`, i.e. `x·g^m + g^n ≤ g^m·g^n`, or `x/g^n ≤ 2κ·g^{−(m+1)}`, i.e. `x·g^{m+1} ≤ 2κ·g^n`. With `2κ + 1 < g^{m+1}` both bounds are below `1`, so the covering radius of the fixed-shell refinement in `[0, 1]` is bounded below at every depth.

E3.name: FRC.Geometry.fixed_shell_floor
E3.doc: 2:E3 — the floor: with `2κ + 1 < g^{m+1}` the second bound `2κ·g^{−(m+1)}` leaves a gap below `1` longer than `1/(2κ+1)`, i.e. `g^{m+1} < (g^{m+1} − 2κ)·(2κ + 1)`; with `g^m ≤ 2κ + 1` the first gap `g^{−m}` is at least `1/(2κ+1)` by hypothesis, so the covering radius is at least `1/(4κ+2) = 1/(p+1)`.

E3.name: FRC.Geometry.fixed_shell_gap
E3.doc: 2:E3 — the fixed-shell gap at `p = 13`, `g = 2` (window `x ≤ 6`): no grid point `x / 2^n` lies strictly between `3/4` and `1` at any depth `n` — the covering radius of the fixed-shell refinement in `[0, 1]` is at least `1/8` for every depth.

E4.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.round_exists
E4.doc: 1:E4, 2:E2, 2:E4 — every framed turn has its rounding (the division with remainder by `2v`).

E4.name: FRC.Geometry.lipschitz_budget
E4.doc: 2:E4 — the budget: `r ≤ L` marked points, each within `d` of its vertex, move an `L`-Lipschitz observable by at most `L·(r·d) ≤ L·(L·d)`, the bound `L²·δ_p` of the operational theorem in counts.

F1.name: FRC.Geometry.principal_root
F1.doc: 2:F1 (Prop. 6.1, root-of-unity facts): `Σ_j g^{jk} = 0` for `0 < k < n`, and `n = card F − 1` reads as `−1` in `F`.

F1.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.principal_root
F1.doc: 2:F1 (Prop. 6.1), 26:B5, 26:H3 — `g` is a principal root of unity: `g^n = 1`, `Σ_{j<n} (g^k)^j = 0` for `0 < k < n`, and `n = p − 1` reads as `−1` in the shell.

F3.name: FRC.Geometry.dft_inverse
F3.doc: 2:F3 (Prop. 6.3, inversion): on every shell the inverse of the Fourier matrix `W_g` (`W k j = g^{jk}`) is `−W_g J`, whose entry at `(k, j)` is `−g^{−jk}`: `W_g · (−W_g J) = 1`.

F3.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.dft_inverse
F3.doc: 2:F3 (Prop. 6.3), 6:B5, 26:H3 — the inversion of the shell Fourier matrix, entrywise: with `W k j = g^{jk}` and `W' l j = −g^{(n−j)l}` (`= −g^{−lj}`), `Σ_{l<n} W k l · W' l j = [k = j]`. The matrix `g^{jk}` on the full cycle `n = p − 1` is both the longitudinal character table (26:B3) and the additive transform on the shell (26:H3).

F5.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.dft_covariance
F5.doc: 2:F5 (Prop. 6.7) — covariance under generator change: for `g' = g^u` (`u` invertible mod `n`) and `v'_j = v_{u·j mod n}`, `F_{g'}(v')_k = F_g(v)_k`.

F6.name: FRC.Geometry.transport_exponents
F6.doc: 2:F6 — the external transport in its exponents: the half-period shifts by `−1`, `g^{m+2κ} = −g^m`; the oriented quarter-turn shifts by three quarters, `i·g^m = g^{m+3κ}` (with `i = −g^κ`, so `χ(i·g^m) = i·χ(g^m)` in the chart); and the kernel, `(g^j)^r = g^{jr}`.
